This section is for maintainers who build the computational environment,
curate the source data, validate outputs, or package a new release. For
analysis of an existing release, start with
[Access the data with Stagecoach](00_access-data.qmd) and the
[reader's guide](00_data-guide.qmd).

The Quarto Manual is the source of truth for pipeline configuration and
command-line tools. It separates three operations:

1. an authoring render produces human-readable documentation;
2. an emission render synchronizes reviewed scripts and configuration;
3. the emitted container runner executes R and the targets pipeline.

No render is permitted to inspect or transform protected source data.
The reader's guide embeds explicitly generated national aggregate figures;
protected source records and clinic-level evidence remain in the governed
workspace. [Evidence maintenance](04_misc-data-guide-evidence.qmd) documents
how operators rebuild those figures and verify their scope.

## Operator workflow

Work through **Setup**, **Infrastructure**, and **Pipeline**, in that order.
Setup establishes the repository contract, rendering boundary, governance,
and migration baseline. Infrastructure constructs the runtime. Pipeline
pages declare source staging, transformations, checks, and release packaging.
Stagecoach owns input staging; tracked notebook parameters own transformation
and release choices.

## Prior Work & Plan

This project has been ongoing for several years, with several hands having
been involved in data management. Contact persons worth keeping in mind:

- Chris Golden (PI, present)
- G. DeNicola (Post Doc, present)
- Marissa Childs (Post Doc, 2024(?))
- Tinashe M. Tapera (RSE, present)

> **Human decision required:** confirm the project participants, their roles,
> and the accountable data steward before source data is staged or inspected.

In general, there are 2 major "blocks" of data: pre-DHIS2, and post.

Pre-implementation of DHSI2, the data were processed ad-hoc and within their means,
and post, the introduction of DHIS2 standards made manual fixes and adjustments
far less prevalent. In our reproduction of the pipeline, we expect
the same truth to hold in implementation. We will keep obvious manual
fixes and patches as they are in the pre-DHIS2 data, as there is little we
can do to confidently improve on spaghetti code without a comparable true
expected outcome to test against. Post DHIS2, we will improve code where
necessary to communicate more clearly, or speed up a laborious task.

## How To Read This Manual

Operator pages combine explanations, procedures, and checks.

Each workflow page follows the [Quarto Manuals page contract](https://goldenplanetaryhealthlab.github.io/QuartoManual/):
one prerequisite block establishes the starting state, one or more procedure
blocks perform the work, and one check block verifies the outcome. Target
declarations, file writes, and execution commands belong in procedures.
Checks inspect the resulting targets or artifacts through assertions,
summaries, plots, or test commands. Read the prose before each code chunk for
its inputs, action, and expected result.

Long transformations are divided into named stages so the operator can
inspect their handoffs. Dependencies between pages live in targets and tracked
files. The public authoring render executes no protected-data analysis;
diagnostic chunks are for an authorized data session, and synthetic tests can
run without the staged sources.

After editing a page, check the block structure without executing its code:

```sh
python3 tests/check-manual-structure.py
```

# Madagascar Healthshed Clinic Data

Monthly clinic-reported counts from Madagascar are distributed with facility
metadata, a diagnosis dictionary, and healthshed geography. Historical
observations cover 2010–2024, with a separately ingested 2025–2026 extension.
These are reported counts; missing measurements are not automatically zeros.

## Accessing and using the data

Follow [Access the data with Stagecoach](notebooks/00_access-data.qmd), then the
[reader's guide](notebooks/00_data-guide.qmd) for file layouts, joins,
missingness, and analysis examples. The dataset is not yet in the Depot.
Use [Stagecoach](https://goldenplanetaryhealthlab.github.io/stagecoach/) to
symlink the shared release directory into your own analysis project:

```text
/n/holylabs/cgolden_lab/Lab/frontier/works/prospectors/prospectorMDGHealthshedClinicData/data/outputs/releases
```

Choose one complete version and retain its `datapackage.json` and provenance
with your analysis. The default package remains an internal candidate;
packaging does not constitute publication.

## Operating the pipeline

The Manual separates operator guidance into Setup, Infrastructure, and
Pipeline. Start with the [operator overview](notebooks/00_cover.qmd).
The Manual owns generated configuration and command-line entry points;
scientific execution occurs explicitly through a Singularity container and
a targets graph. Historical curation, the separate 2025–2026 extension,
validation, and immutable Parquet packaging with a Frictionless descriptor
are implemented. Full archived measurement equivalence and publication
remain separate review decisions.

Only the reviewed national aggregate figures and their comparison summaries
are included in the Manual; protected source records and clinic-level
evidence remain outside the rendered Manual and version control.

## Render the Manual

```sh
scripts/render-isolated --profile authoring
scripts/render-isolated --profile emit
```

The authoring profile updates the rendered Manual. The emit profile also
synchronizes generated scripts and configuration from reviewed `.qmd` source.

## Build and operate the environment

Follow the rendered Infrastructure pages in `docs/infrastructure/`. After the
runtime image and frozen R library exist:

```sh
scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data
scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec uvr run scripts/run-pipeline.R
```

With no subcommand, the container runner opens a shell in the repository.
Commands require the explicit `exec` subcommand.
